newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia share volume up but Kaija slips.
newsitem.headline: Latvia share volume up but Kaija slips.

text.p: The Latvian stock market's total trade gained on Tuesday although several leading stocks fell, dealers said.
The Rietumu Bank index lost 1.32 percent to 174.21 while market trade was 72,000 lats versus around 50,000 lats.
Kaija, its first day on the official list, lost 8.9 percent to 2.35 lats on 6,800 lats trade after rising sharply on Monday.
"Kaija is now returning to its normal price after a speculative jump," said Harijs Zulgis, Rigas komercbanka dealer.
Riga Shipyard, spending its second day on the bourse after beginning quotations yesterday, slipped three santimes to 1.40 lats on turnover of 3,700 lats.
Some dealers said the market was expected to stay quiet until companies release first-half results.
"There is no fresh money, a narrowing of the market is taking place as lots of funds have left the bourse ahead of big utility privatisations," said Leonid Ruderman, a dealer with Pareks Bank.
"We can expect more activity when half-year figures come in. The market has grown cleverer and is now carefully evaluating quarterly results," Ruderman said.
Daugavpils Chain was most traded on 28,600 lats for a rise of four santimes to 2.40 lats ahead of an expected share isse of 84 shares for every 100 held.
Unibanka was slightly lower at 3.47 lats versus 3.50 lats and Staburadze gained 1.5 percent to 2.69 lats.
